newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 index back on rollercoaster track.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 index back on rollercoaster track.

text.p: Belgium's Bel-20 leading share index, feeling refreshed after a four-day breather, moved into gear again on Friday for the next stage of its rollercoaster ride, dealers said.
The Bel-20 capped a four-day barren run with a 0.68 percent rise to 2,361.64 points on a cocktail of June options expiry and bonds and dollar strength.
"We've put one step backwards and now we're putting three or four steps forwards again. We just don't know the strength of this driving force," said Pieter Vander Stichele at Generale Bank.

Vander Stichele said the market was likely to edge higher until the 1997 half-year earnings season starting at the end of August, the only factor which now appeared to have the potential to shake-up the market.

He said the Bel-20 was initially driven up by the expiry -- with first 300 and then 202 baskets passed right after the fixing at 1300 GMT. "But at the same time the dollar gained ground and Bunds also moved into positive territory," he added.
The Bel-20 quickly shot up to 2,368 points from 2,352 but ran out of steam towards the end of trade.
Bank BBL was the most prominent Bel-20 loser.

BBL closed 1.1 percent or 110 francs lower after chief executive officer Michel Tilmant said in magazine interview Thursday that the so-called Great Belgian bank project was on hold. It had already shed 140 francs on Thursday.
Holding company GBL, which owns a direct stake of around 12.4 percent in BBL, dipped 0.2 percent to 5,960.
Another bank, Kredietbank, added 0.2 percent after a selling wave sparked by a newspaper interview in which it said it preferred to stay independent, just like BBL.
One dealer said the big banks were playing a game of chess and merely stressing their independence "to drive up the price".

Chemicals and drugs firm UCB, which soared to a June 13 record of 122,000 francs before sliding to a close of 112,900 on Thursday, exemplified the change of heart of the Bel-20 by adding 2.5 percent to 115,750 francs.
